item.title: [News] Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest: Artist in Residence Programme 2027 (USA)
item.description:
Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest’s artist in residence programme annually awards artists the opportunity to live and create site-specific work inspired by their total immersion experience in the natural environment.

The residency is open to visual and mixed-media artists, including those working with sound and performance art that incorporates visual elements.

Bernheim recommends a stay of 6–8 weeks, but the residency can be split into two periods, with a minimum of three weeks per period. While full immersion is preferred, flexibility is available.

Artists will create a site-inspired artwork, temporary installation, or project as a donation to the Bernheim Foundation. Recipients are also asked to engage the public with their work and process, which may include demonstrations, workshops, lectures, and participation in one of Bernheim’s programs or annual events.

The programme provides the following:

  • 2,500 USD stipend
  • Furnished, one-bedroom rustic cabin with a full kitchen, bath, and Wi-Fi
  • Modest studio space with good natural light and heating, situated near a 32-acre lake.
  • Support and guidance from Bernheim’s horticulture and operations departments, as well as staff ecologists, scientists, naturalists, and forest managers, are available for Artist-in-Residence projects
  • Access to free or heavily discounted classes, workshops, night walks, and other activities during the residency
  • Participation in high-profile public and private events designed to promote artists and the Arts in Nature programme
Deadline: 30 November 2026

More info and apply: https://bernheim.org/news/call-for-2027-artist-in-residence/

item.title: [News] European Hybrid Intelligence Network: Dirtly Lab Residencies 2027 (Belgium, Croatia, Germany, Serbia, Slovenia, Spain)
item.description:
EHIN (the European Hybrid Intelligence Network) has announced its Open Call for Artists’ Residencies. This programme brings together artists, scientists and field practitioners to explore hybrid intelligence, embedded between different species and in living systems, and biocomputing as a creative and ecological alternative to energy-intensive, silicon-based technologies.

EHIN is a programme designed to support six artists through a two-phase, cross-institutional residency, running for approximately 12 months per artist, starting from February 2027.

Through six Dirtly Lab residencies, hosted by six partner institutions across Europe, EHIN offers artists the opportunity to develop a new artwork in direct collaboration with scientists in the field of hybrid intelligence and bio-computation and a local field practitioner (such as a herbalist, farmer, or ecologist), supported by dedicated production teams and access to specialised infrastructure.

Each residency pairs 1 artist + 1 scientist/expert + 1 field practitioner. The six host partners are: Kersnikova Institute (Slovenia), CPN (Serbia), GLUON (Belgium), LABoral (Spain), ZKM (Germany), and KONTEJNER (Croatia)

Each residency includes at least 2 Open Dirty Labs of public engagement activities, sharing the artistic and scientific process with local communities.

Support includes the following:

  • Up to 25,000 EUR budget per residency, covering artist fee and production costs
  • Travel and accommodation costs are arranged separately in agreement with the host institution(s) for both residency phases
  • Curatorial guidance and production support
  • Access to biocomputing experts and local field practitioners
  • A second co-production phase at a partner institution
  • Public presentation of the resulting artwork in a solo exhibition or group show
Deadline: 4 December 2026

More info and apply: https://europeanhybridintelligencenetwork.eu/open-call/

item.title: [News] IN SITU: Online Support and Immersive Lab for Emerging Artists Creating in Public Space (3rd Call)
item.description:
IN SITU is now calling for applications from emerging artists creating in public space for their third open call. Around 60 European artists will have access to online content to learn about artistic production related to art in public space from March to June 2027 and an in-person immersive lab with learning and networking opportunities (May to September 2027).

Online content includes:

  • Three online support sessions with On the Move
  • Two to six peer-to-peer exchange sessions with experienced IN SITU artists
  • Short videos and online webinars to learn from IN SITU programmers and artists

An immersive lab is an artistic seminar designed for IN SITU emerging artists to provide food for thoughts to nourish their artistic projects. These six-day gatherings take place during an event or festival hosted by one of the IN SITU partners and bring together around 15 artists at a time

This open call is for artistic proposals in development. The project should:

  • have not yet premiered or toured;
  • be further progressed than the ideas stage;
  • be intended for presentation in public space or non-conventional venues;
  • have the potential to be presented to an audience around summer 2028.

The costs covered for the participation in the immersive lab include: a writing aid fee of 1,500 EUR including taxes, plus travel up to 300 EUR roundtrip for air travel, meals, and accommodation. Maximum two artists from a collective can attend a lab.

IN SITU will then directly support around 10 of the selected projects with production residencies. The programme will culminate in a FOCUS event in the summer of 2028, taking place in the context of La Strada Graz in Austria.

Deadline: 9 December 2026

More info and apply: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qjTiTVucBt_GBuPNP3FY6NOC0Z0Uul8Q/view
